claims.claim: **At every age, sunlight is the main source of vitamin D.** Australian cases of nutritional rickets are generally confined to dark-skinned infants and children.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Breastmilk has almost no vitamin D**, whereas infant formula is fortified.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recommended intake without sun exposure:** 0–12 months 400 units daily; 1–18 years 400–600 units daily.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Status by 25-OH-D:** severe deficiency under 12.5 nmol/L · moderate 12.5–29 · mild 30–49 · **sufficient 50 or more (the target at all ages)** · elevated 250 or more. **Toxicity = over 250 nmol/L with hypercalcaemia and PTH suppression.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Risk factors:** little sun exposure (time indoors, covering clothes), dark skin, conditions that alter vitamin D metabolism (medications, severe malabsorption, liver/renal failure, obesity); **infants: exclusive breastfeeding plus** any of these, maternal deficiency or prematurity.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Low-calcium symptoms:** tetany, muscle cramps, stridor, seizures (seizures are rare after 6–12 months of age).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Signs of rickets:** long-bone deformity, widened wrists/ankles, late closure of the anterior fontanelle (normally shut by 2 years), frontal bossing, rachitic rosary, increased fracture risk; also late dentition (still toothless at 9 months, or molar-free at 14 months).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider admission for severe rickets or symptomatic hypocalcaemia (tetany, stridor, seizures).** Refer for specialist review: clinical rickets · an infant with symptoms/signs · abnormal serum calcium · deficiency not responding to high-dose supplements.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A breastfed infant under 12 months who has other risk factors but no symptoms or signs can usually start 400 units daily untested.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Any child/adolescent with at least one risk factor: screen with 25-OH-D, calcium, phosphate, ALP**; add PTH when there are symptoms, several risk factors or a low calcium intake. **Rickets:** add Mg, PTH, UEC, urine studies and a left wrist X-ray.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat low vitamin D to restore levels to 50 nmol/L or more**, ensure adequate calcium intake, and educate on sun exposure. Evidence for high-dose treatment under 3 months is limited.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Preterm:** 200 units/kg/day when mild (30–49 nmol/L), max 400 units/day (same for maintenance); moderate–severe (under 30) 800 units/day, review after 1 month.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Term, under 3 months:** mild 400 units/day for 3 months (then 400 units daily); moderate–severe 1,000 units/day for 3 months.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **3–12 months:** mild 400 units/day for 3 months (then 400 units daily); moderate–severe, 3 months of 1,000 units/day **or** a stat 50,000 units, review after 1 month and consider repeating.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **1–18 years, mild (30–49):** 3 months of 1,000–2,000 units/day, **or** a stat 150,000 units. **Maintenance:** 400–600 units a day, **or** 3000–4000 units a week, **or** 150,000 units as autumn begins.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **1–18 years, moderate–severe (under 30):** 6 months of 1,000–2,000 units daily, **or** 3 months of 3,000–4,000 units daily, **or** a stat 150,000 units, repeated at 6 weeks.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Nutritional rickets: specialist-guided; minimum vitamin D 2000 units daily for at least 3 months plus oral calcium 500 mg daily** (diet or supplement); phosphate may also be needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Check which product the family uses** — **overdose can happen**, as some preparations contain 1000 units per drop; most adult tablets are 1000 units.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **At-risk breastfed infants: vitamin D 400 units a day, for the first 12 months at least.** Fully formula-fed infants usually need no supplement.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Repeat bloods:** not usually needed in mild deficiency; otherwise at 1 month in infants, 3 months if older.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Self-management plan:** over the cooler months (May–August), consider 400–600 units a day **or** 3000–4000 units a week to avoid blood tests and high-dose therapy.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sun:** normal sunscreen use does not cause low vitamin D; children with dark skin can tolerate intermittent sun without sunscreen (hat and sunglasses still recommended). In winter in southern Australia, sun alone may not maintain levels.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vitamin D deficiency' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vitamin_D_deficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23
